stem: During a teaching discussion on normal dental development, a student asks why permanent teeth can provide clues about early postnatal health. What is the best explanation?

options.text: Permanent teeth first begin developing at age 3 years
Primary teeth erupt between 6 and 18 years
Permanent tooth eruption is complete by age 3 years
Only unilateral tooth eruption is considered normal

explanation: Permanent teeth calcify from birth. This means their development reflects early postnatal growth and health, whereas the other options describe incorrect timelines or a false normal variant.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes

rationale: Permanent teeth begin developing in utero and calcify from birth, which is why they can help indicate early postnatal health.

optionExplanations.A: Correct because permanent teeth calcify from birth, allowing early postnatal influences to be reflected in their development.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because permanent teeth begin developing before birth, not at age 3 years.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because primary teeth erupt in early childhood, not between 6 and 18 years.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because permanent tooth eruption continues through childhood and adolescence, not by age 3 years.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because unilateral eruption is not considered a normal defining feature of tooth development.
